parsedVerdict.reasoning: This module has one job: removing sensitive values from HTTP responses for viewers with restricted access. The interceptor file holds all of the logic. It does not write its own permission checks or redaction code. It calls the shared helpers `hasReadRestrictedAccessPermission`, `isRestrictedView` and `redactPaths`, and reads the shared constant `DEFAULT_REDACTED_PATHS`. So the rule for when and what to redact is defined in one place. The module file is an empty NestJS wrapper (`@Module({})`) that lets feature modules import this one. It adds no competing behaviour and goes around nothing. The rule is not broken: the module serves one concern, uses its abstractions consistently, and repeats no rule.
